rationale: Answers the last open half of the trim child's gap from the shipped storage implementation, so that nothing in the audit is left as an unexamined unknown beyond what genuinely needs a new run. MemoryStorage::get_entries, get_suffix and trim all subtract self.trimmed_idx from the caller-supplied index without a guard (memory_storage.rs 92-107 and 122-127), so a caller that asks for a prefix below the trimmed index behaves in one of exactly two ways depending on the build: under overflow checks, which is the profile every receipt in this run was built with (the cargo artifacts record overflow_checks true), the subtraction panics; with overflow checks disabled, where usize arithmetic wraps, the wrapped index lands past the end of the log, log.get(...) returns None, and the call returns an empty vector - the silently empty suffix the gap named as the other possibility. The storage trait leaves that out-of-range case to the implementer, so the answer is a property of the shipped implementation and the profile rather than a library-level guarantee, and it stays source-derived: no execution in this run asked the storage for a prefix below a compacted index. The account is rewritten as a successor with that finding in its answer, its limitations and its knowledge uses, and a new knowledge entry records the storage behaviour itself; no execution was requested and no other record changed.

knowledge.statement: MemoryStorage::get_entries and get_suffix subtract self.trimmed_idx from the caller-supplied index without any guard, and trim subtracts it in the same way when computing how much to drain: a request for a prefix below the trimmed index therefore panics on the subtraction in an overflow-checked build, and when overflow checks are disabled the subtraction wraps, the wrapped index lands past the end of the log, log.get returns None and the read reports an empty result - the silently empty suffix rather than an error. The same shape applies to trim, where the wrapped value is then clamped by min(log.len()).
knowledge.conditions: Any call into the shipped in-memory storage with an index below the index it has already trimmed to, whatever the caller: the library's own log-sync path is closed to that case inside a cluster (the trim bound is the minimum recorded accepted index and the snapshot path takes its own branch), so the remaining callers are direct users of the Storage trait or storage implementations' own code. Observed by reading memory_storage.rs 92-107 (get_entries, get_suffix) and 122-127 (trim); not executed in this run, and other implementations of the trait may differ in either direction.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed and bounded, with the second producer recorded, the suffix route split by source and execution, and the storage-level half now answered from the shipped implementation. The trim witness stands: with recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content and every node's decided report at 9, trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7, past the leader's own content, after which its reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15). The discriminator this question carried asked whether a producer other than trim can raise a compacted index past a replica's content, and the snapshot receipt answers that it can: with the same drifted state, snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the leader's compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). That second producer needs no recorded accepted index at all - its bound is the leader's decided index - so a drift confined to the decided index would be enough for it, while trim additionally needs the drifted value to be the configuration's minimum recorded accepted index; both are bounded by values the leader derives for itself. Correction review: the drift knowledge this account cites was narrowed to revision 2, which keeps the half this account needs - the reported accepted index drifts one further index per re-synchronization round, inflating exactly the recorded accepted indexes the trim bound is derived from - and bounds the decided index to the rounds in which a write quorum of drifted reports covers it; this account reads its decided values from its own receipt's samples, so the narrowing leaves its conclusion unchanged, and the use is re-read at revision 2 below. The suffix route, in three parts. Executed in-cluster: in the snapshot-capable sibling case the lagging replica re-synchronized below the leader's compacted index (the leader had compacted to 8 with a snapshot holding zero ids) was not refused and did not panic - it received that complete snapshot and no suffix, reported accepted 10 / decided 10 and read two decided entries where the configuration decided six (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162). Closed by source: a request below a trim-produced compacted index cannot arise inside the cluster, because the trim bound is the minimum over the leader's accepted_indexes vector and that vector carries an entry for every configuration member from the start (get_min_all_accepted_idx, util.rs 186-191, whose expect message reads Should be all initialised to 0, and set_promise rewrites the sender's entry on every promise), so only a replica's own inflation moves the bound. Answered for the shipped storage: a caller that does ask the storage for a prefix below its trimmed index gets one of two outcomes depending only on the build profile, because MemoryStorage::get_entries and get_suffix subtract self.trimmed_idx unguarded (memory_storage.rs 92-107) and trim does the same (122-127) - under overflow checks the subtraction panics, and with overflow checks disabled it wraps past the end of the log and the read reports an empty result, the silently empty suffix the gap named; the trait leaves that case to the implementer, so the answer is a property of this implementation and profile rather than a library guarantee. The abort this lineage did observe belongs to a different entry point, the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance (40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-question-1).

b26c13954e184cd2b9fdfda975aff136-gap-4.explanation: Answered in substance for every route the gap names, though not by an execution of the storage-level case itself, so it stays open. In-cluster (executed): a replica re-synchronizing below a compacted index does not panic - it is handed a complete snapshot built from the empty part of the log and a shortened decided log (receipt 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162, guarded result event 162 with panicked false). A peer compacted while its recorded values were still truthful (closed by source): impossible, because the trim bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes over a per-node vector that is initialised for every member, so a truthful replica keeps the bound at or below its own accepted index. A store-level trim or a direct range read below a compacted index (answered for the shipped implementation, still unexecuted): MemoryStorage::get_entries and get_suffix subtract self.trimmed_idx without a guard, so the request panics under overflow checks - the profile every receipt in this run was built with - and wraps past the end of the log to an empty read when overflow checks are disabled, which is the silently empty suffix the gap asked about; the trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer, so another storage may answer differently in either direction. The only thing left is whether a given implementation and build profile exhibits the panic or the empty result.

ebbec352695d43beb398bb1b239cda41-gap-6.explanation: The narrowed knowledge retains the drift of the reported accepted index, which is the half this account relies on: the trim bound is the minimum of the recorded accepted indexes, so what matters here is that each re-synchronization raises the reported accepted index by one index over unchanged content, and the account reads the decided values from its own receipt's samples rather than from the assumption that the decided index keeps following the drift. The conclusion, the witness and the content comparison are therefore unchanged; the knowledge use is re-read at revision 2.

ebbec352695d43beb398bb1b239cda41-gap-8.explanation: Same review as the sibling note for this knowledge revision: this account uses the drift of the reported accepted index (the trim bound's input) and its own sampled decided values, not the unbounded following of the decided index that the correction narrowed, so the correction does not change the conclusion or the witness, and the knowledge use is re-read at revision 2.

knowledge.assertion: trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
trim's bound is the minimum over a per-node recorded accepted vector, so a truthful replica keeps it at or below its own accepted index
the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it
a replica re-synchronized below the compacted index receives a complete snapshot built from the empty range

counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented all-decided precondition was satisfied only in the drifted bookkeeping; the obligation I rely on is that the compacted index must not exceed the entries the leader holds, which it did (7 for trim, 8 for the snapshot).
The trim call returned Ok, so nothing in its own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.

The in-cluster route below a compacted index is now executed rather than argued, and it does not abort: the lagging replica was re-synchronized with a complete but empty snapshot and a shortened decided log (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 161, 162), so the over-compaction of this account leads to a silent loss on a lagging replica; the abort seen in the same lineage belongs to the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance and is recorded under its own question.

The peer-side sub-route is closed by source rather than merely untested: a truthful replica's recorded accepted index stays in the minimum the trim bound is taken from, so the bound cannot pass such a replica and no request below the compacted index follows from it.

The storage-level answer is a property of the shipped implementation and the build profile, not of the library: the trait leaves out-of-range reads to the implementer, so a different storage could refuse, panic or return empty where MemoryStorage does one of the latter two.
limitations: The trim over-compaction is bounded to replicas whose recorded accepted index has drifted; a truthful replica would have kept the bound lower, and the per-node initialisation of the recorded vector is the reason.

The storage-level half of the suffix question is read from the shipped implementation rather than executed: MemoryStorage subtracts the trimmed index unguarded in get_entries, get_suffix and trim, so the outcome depends on overflow checks being enabled in the build (panicking) or not (wrapping to an empty read); no run asked the storage for a prefix below a compacted index, and other implementations may differ.
The baseline comparisons of both receipts are unknown because they were admitted through event names shared across cases in one execution; those states are asserted from the sampled operands.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change for trim and one snapshot-capable entry type were exercised; the peers that receive a forwarded compaction were not sampled beyond their accepted and decided indexes, and the lagging-replica outcome was observed with the leader's log empty above its compacted index.

For the trim path the observed over-compaction is the minimum of the drifted recorded values, so the number of indices it passes beyond the leader's content depends on how many rounds each replica drifted; only one such combination was sampled.

The initialisation claim for the recorded accepted vector is read from the source's own expect message and from set_promise rewriting the sender's entry; no execution sampled the vector directly or ran a trim while one member had never promised.
